newsitem.title: USA: Prudential said reducing New York commodity staff.
newsitem.headline: Prudential said reducing New York commodity staff.

text.p: In a bid to cut costs, the brokerage house Prudential Securities will close its floor operations at some New York commodity exchanges, Prudential sources said Friday.
The move will result in 25 to 30 job cuts in the commodities trading areas, particularly in metals and so-called "soft" commodities, such as cocoa, coffee and orange juice.
The oil trading desk on the New York Mercantile Exchange might be beefed up, however, according to Prudential traders who spoke on condition of not being named.

A Prudential Securities spokeman would not comment on whether the company intended to lay off any floor traders, but maintained that the firm was "absolutely committed to keeping our presence on the floor."
The job cuts, which will take effect in about two weeks, were viewed as mainly a cost-cutting measure, one Prudential floor trader said.
"Their excuse is we are not making money," the trader said.
In the past year, other investment firms such as Merrill Lynch and J. Aron, a division of Goldman, Sachs & Co., have moved to cut costs by scaling back floor trading operations.
"I think there is a trend to more closely scrutinise floor staffs," one industry source said. "People get tired of not making any money and are getting rid of their head count."
